chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Miskan, from Abi Basir, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about wudu (ablution), and he said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would perform wudu (ablution) with one mudd and perform ghusl with one sa'.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before certain acts of worship
key_terms.بِصَاعٍ: with one sa', a known measure of volume
key_terms.بِمُدٍّ: with one mudd, a known measure of volume
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he would perform ghusl, the ritual bath

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for wudu (ablution) and ghusl according to the sunnah (prophetic tradition)?
ai.summary: This hadith states the amount of water with which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to perform wudu (ablution) and ghusl. It serves as evidence in rulings of ritual purity and demonstrates the Prophetic sunnah (tradition) of moderation in water use for acts of worship.
